question: I have a $2 \times 4$ grid of squares. How many ways can I shade at least one of the squares such that no two shaded squares share an edge?

spans.label: [SYMBOLIZATION.DIRECT-MAPPING]
spans.text: That means if I shade a square, I can't shade any square that's directly next to it horizontally or vertically. Diagonally is okay, right? Because diagonally adjacent squares don't share an edge. So,

spans.text:
since the problem says "at least one," I need to consider all possible subsets of squares that satisfy the non-adjacent condition, except the empty set.
